question: What is the percentage of patient who has a abnormal level of glutamic oxaloacetic transaminase level, yet he or she is diagnosed with SLE?
evidence: abnormal level of glutamic oxaloacetic transaminase refers to GOT > = 60; percentage = MULTIPLY(DIVIDE(COUNT(ID WHERE GOT > = 60 AND Diagnosis = 'SLE'), COUNT(ID WHERE GOT > = 60)), 1.0);
clarification: Count each distinct CASE WHEN Diagnosis LIKE '%SLE%' THEN ID ELSE 0 END only once.
gold: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN T1.Diagnosis LIKE '%SLE%' THEN T1.ID ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(T1.ID) FROM Patient AS T1 INNER JOIN Laboratory AS T2 ON T1.ID = T2.ID WHERE T2."GOT" >= 60
gold0: SELECT COUNT(CASE WHEN T1.Diagnosis LIKE '%SLE%' THEN T1.ID ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(T1.ID) FROM Patient AS T1 INNER JOIN Laboratory AS T2 ON T1.ID = T2.ID WHERE T2.`GOT` >= 60

c.sql: SELECT 1.0 * COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN P.Diagnosis LIKE '%SLE%' THEN L.ID END) / NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT L.ID), 0) AS percentage FROM Laboratory AS L JOIN Patient AS P ON P.ID = L.ID WHERE L.GOT >= 60;

b.request: Among distinct patients with at least one GOT reading of 60 or higher, what percentage have a Patient diagnosis containing “SLE”?
b.sql: SELECT 100.0 * COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN p.Diagnosis LIKE '%SLE%' THEN p.ID END) / NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT p.ID), 0) AS percentage FROM Patient AS p JOIN Laboratory AS l ON l.ID = p.ID WHERE l.GOT >= 60;

d.request: What percentage of patients with a GOT level of at least 60 have a diagnosis containing “SLE,” counting each qualifying patient ID only once?
d.sql: SELECT 100.0 * COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN p.Diagnosis LIKE '%SLE%' THEN p.ID END) / NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT p.ID), 0) AS percentage FROM Patient AS p JOIN Laboratory AS l ON l.ID = p.ID WHERE l.GOT >= 60;
